segments.narration: A Maya book called fake for decades is the oldest. Ten bark-paper pages, an almanac tracking Venus, radiocarbon dated to between 1021 and 1154 AD.
Its arrival helped nobody believe it. A collector said he was flown in 1965 to an airstrip in Tabasco and shown the thing there.
No excavation records, no site, no paperwork at all. How do you ever prove a looted book is genuine?
Chemistry did it. Mexico's INAH found gypsum-prepared paper and pigments of lamp black, hematite red and Maya blue, all aged together with the sheets.
In 2018 INAH declared the codex authentic and renamed it the Codice Maya de Mexico, the oldest surviving book anywhere in the Americas.
